subject: Question on ind and replicate argument in bilat.symmetry

messages.author: 6180ccabbdf86586
messages.subject: Question on ind and replicate argument in bilat.symmetry
parts:
Hello everyone,

I want to examine shape changes of individuals of object symmetry over 3 time periods. For example, I have 3 individuals and each individual is measured at baseline, 5 years later, and 10 years later. I arrange coordinates for individuals in the following order: the first 3 datasets are coordinates for individual 1 measured at baseline, 5, and 10 year in this order, then another 3 datasets for the 2nd and 3rd individual.

I tried bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = (rep("ind1", 3), rep("ind2", 3), rep("ind3", 3)) , object.sym = TRUE, land.pairs = land.pairs, data = data3, replicate = replicate = rep(1:3, 3), RRPP = TRUE). This gave me one procrustes dataset for each specimen (3 dataset rather than 9 in total), suggesting data for the same ind were merged. So should I instead set ind = 1:9 so that measurements at different times on the same individual are considered as a different ind in bilat.symmetry in my case?

Thank you.
Kieran

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Question on ind and replicate argument in bilat.symmetry
parts:
Kieran,

 

The way you have set up the symmetry analysis does not correspond with your question. It sounds as if you wish to treat each individual at each time point as a separate object. But you have used ind=rep(1,3), … in the formula. That tells the analysis that an individual is replicated 3 times, and of course will find an overall average of them for the symmetric and asymmetric components.

 

To do what you seem to want, you need to treat each individual at each time point as a separate object. That means using: ind <- seq(1:9), and using no ‘rep’ component.

 

Obviously, the summary anova table in this case is meaningless, but this will give you the symmetric and asymmetric components of shape for each individual.

 

Dean
